title: The Quiet Flat
summary: The first three days after Lisa leaves. Starts fully black; ends with 3 lights. Unlocks Chapter 2 after the quest at 1.40.

screens.image: Fully black. A single cream title in hand lettering.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: After.

screens.image: Black.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: This is Théo. You can't see him yet. That's how it is right now.

screens.image: A thin pale outline fades in: Théo sitting on a kitchen floor, back against the cupboards.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Théo is twenty-six. He is sitting on the kitchen floor, which is not where people usually sit.

screens.image: Close-up: a door, closed. A blue suitcase wheel mark on the floor.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: An hour ago, Lisa took her blue suitcase and closed the door very gently. That was the worst part. The gentleness.

screens.image: A faint outline of a trophy, a guitar, a diploma and a shop sign on a shelf, all in shadow.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: It's the second thing to end this year. Since he was fifteen, Théo had one plan. This spring, it quietly stopped being possible.

screens.image: The shelf again, the {chasedObject} slightly clearer, the rest gone.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: And now: a shelf, and a man on a kitchen floor who doesn't know what comes next.

screens.image: The dark kitchen, outlines of: a mug, a plant, a note on the fridge, a pot on the stove.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: The flat is the same flat. Same kettle. Same crack in the ceiling shaped like Italy. But the sound has gone out of it.

objects.label: Mug
objects.line: Her mug. Théo leaves it exactly where it is.

objects.label: Plant
objects.line: Her plant. He doesn't know how often it needs water. She always knew.

objects.label: Fridge note
objects.line: "Buy oat milk." He will not be buying oat milk.

objects.label: Pot
objects.line: Soup. The one she liked. Made for two.

screens.image: The Critic appears for the first time in the corner, size 5.

words.speaker: Critic
words.text: Of course she left. And the plan's gone too. What's left, exactly?

screens.image: Théo's outline, head on knees.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Nothing needs answering tonight. Tonight, Théo only has to get through the next hour.

options.label: Lie on the floor and breathe

image.water: The chosen action in outline: a glass of water.
image.window: The chosen action in outline: a window with cold air lines.
image.floor: The chosen action in outline: Théo flat on the floor.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: That counts. That's all tonight asks.

screens.image: Black, with a small cream "Day two" in the corner. Thick panel gutters.
screens.caption: Day two

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Day two. Théo doesn't eat. He isn't refusing to. His body has simply stopped being hungry.

screens.image: The pot on the stove, a skin on the soup.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: This happens in the first days of grief. Bodies go quiet. It passes.

screens.image: Théo in bed in the dark, his face lit cold blue by his phone. Nothing else in the room is lit.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: He looks at her photos. The screen is very bright and lights nothing at all.

screens.image: Same, the blue glow larger, Théo smaller.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Théo feels worse. He knew he would. That's not a crime.

screens.image: Phone face down. Total black.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: The dark is very dark. But it's his own.

screens.image: Evening. Black flat. A sound-effect in cream letters: knock.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: A knock. Théo doesn't move. A second knock.

screens.image: Door open. Warm yellow light from the stairwell pours across the black floor. Madame Roux in slippers, holding a container.

words.speaker: Madame Roux
words.text: I saw her suitcase on the stairs.

screens.image: Close on the container in her hands, glowing softly.

words.speaker: Madame Roux
words.text: Soupe de légumes, made this morning. You always bring me things. Three spoons. Not for you. For me.

screens.image: The door closes, but the container in Théo's hands keeps a small glow.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: She doesn't ask anything else. She just goes back downstairs.

screens.image: Théo standing at the counter, eating from the container. The glow on his face now.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Théo eats three spoons standing up. Then four. It's the first warm thing in two days.

screens.image: Black page, one warm point: the container.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: That was the first light. Notice it didn't come from inside Théo. Not yet. It came up the stairs in slippers.

screens.image: Black. "Day three" in the corner. Phone buzzing on the counter.
screens.caption: Day three

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Day three. His phone buzzes.

screens.image: The phone screen, warm yellow this time: a message from Camille.

words.speaker: Camille
words.text: thinking of you. no need to answer.

screens.image: Théo holding the warm phone.
A desk drawer opening: paper, an envelope, a stick of red wax.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Before his appointment, Théo does something odd. He writes to someone who doesn't exist yet: the Théo of later.

screens.image: Paper on the table, a pen.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: What does today's Théo want later's Théo to know?

screens.image: The sealed envelope in a drawer, the drawer closing.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Sealed. Later's Théo will read it. Today's Théo just has to get there.

screens.image: A street at morning, everything black, Théo's outline walking with his hood up.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: He almost cancels his appointment. He types the message twice and deletes it twice. Cancelling would mean explaining.

screens.image: Marie-Clo's office: two chairs, one plant, a box of tissues on a low table. A small desk lamp gives a warm glow.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Marie-Clo's office has one plant, two chairs, and a box of tissues Théo is determined not to touch.

screens.image: Marie-Clo in her chair, cup of tea.

words.speaker: Marie-Clo
words.text: So. Tell me about the week.

screens.image: A clock on the wall: four minutes.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Théo tells her. It takes four minutes. It felt like it should take longer.

screens.image: Marie-Clo leaning forward slightly.

words.speaker: Marie-Clo
words.text: Can I give you some homework you'll probably hate?

screens.image: Marie-Clo's hands drawing a small circle in the air; inside it, a tiny Théo in a tiny flat.

words.speaker: Marie-Clo
words.text: Right now your whole world is the size of your flat and your head. Be interested in other people. Not to fix yourself. Just to see what's out there.

screens.image: Marie-Clo smiling slightly.

words.speaker: Marie-Clo
words.text: One person. One real question. Then come back and tell me what you learned about them. Not about you.

screens.image: Théo looking unconvinced.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Théo thinks this is a bit simple. He doesn't say so.

screens.image: Théo on the street again; the street still black, but the lamp glow from Marie-Clo's window behind him.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: It was simple. Simple and easy aren't the same thing.

screens.image: A small notebook appears, cream cover, title "People".

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: The curiosity notebook. Each page is for someone else's life.

screens.image: Black skyline from Théo's window. Three tiny warm points: Madame Roux's window, his phone, Marie-Clo's window.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Three lights. It doesn't sound like much. A few days ago, there were none.

screens.image: The Critic, still big, sitting on the windowsill.

words.speaker: Critic
words.text: Three lights. Pathetic.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: The Critic will talk a lot in this story. Théo doesn't have to believe it.

screens.image: End-of-chapter card: a hand-drawn soup bowl.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: End of Chapter 1.

screens.image: Quest card.

interaction.title: One real question
interaction.text: Ask one person one real question this week (a cashier, a colleague, a neighbour, family). Then write one thing you learned about them.

notebook.textPrompt: One thing you learned about them
